Two flight attendants report injuries and one of them is taken to a hospital

LOS ANGELES, USA – Actor Selma Blair has been arrested after flight attendants reported a “physically abusive passenger” on a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to New York, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey’s police department said on Monday, October 12.
Police identified Blair, known for roles in the movies “Cruel Intentions” and “Hellboy,” as the suspect in an incident on Sunday evening, October 11.

She was taken into custody at New York’s John F. Kennedy Airport and transported to a hospital for evaluation, police said in a statement. Two flight attendants reported injuries and one of them was taken to a hospital, according to the statement.
A representative for 54-year-old Blair said she had a medical emergency during the flight.
“Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct,” Blair’s representative said. “Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition.”
Blair has spoken publicly about her battle with multiple sclerosis. She was diagnosed with the autoimmune disorder in 2018. – Rappler.com

articles.title: P41-million withdrawal from Mans Carpio’s accounts in 73 minutes ‘unusual' — witness
articles.summary: A forensic accountant has described as “unusual” the withdrawal of P41 million in cash from the bank accounts of Vice President Sara Duterte's husband, Mans Carpio, within an hour and 13…

blocks.text: October 13, 2026 | 9:13am

MANILA, Philippines — A forensic accountant has described as “unusual” the withdrawal of P41 million in cash from the bank accounts of Vice President Sara Duterte's husband, Mans Carpio, within an hour and 13 minutes on Aug. 6, 2024, saying the closely timed transactions appeared rushed.

Responding to Sen. Risa Hontiveros’ questions during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, October 12, forensic accountant Alexander Cabrera said the amount and timing of the withdrawals raised questions.
“Sa ordinaryong tao po, unusual po. Eh 41 million in cash, kailangan n'yo po siyempre ng bag po doon. And parang may hinahabol po eh, kasi lahat po ginawa within the hour po,” he said.
(For an ordinary person, that would be unusual. P41 million in cash would, of course, require a bag to carry. And it seemed like they were in a hurry because everything was done within an hour.)
Hontiveros cited Table 24, page 18 of Cabrera’s forensic report, which recorded the total cash withdrawals of P41 million on Aug. 6, 2024.

Cabrera confirmed that both accounts involved in the transactions belonged to Carpio. He questioned why such a large amount was withdrawn in cash instead of being transferred to another bank account or obtained through a manager’s check.
He said the absence of supporting documents could also serve as evidence in a forensic investigation, particularly when a transaction took place without a clear paper trail.

“Pagka po ‘yung mga transactions po kulang sa trail, kulang sa record, wala pong document evidencing it pero nangyari po yung transaction, yung pong walang document nangyari yung transaction, evidence din po ‘yun eh,” Cabrera said.
(When transactions lack a trail, lack records and have no documents to support them, but the transactions still took place, the absence of documentation is also evidence.)
His team also examined the timestamps of the withdrawals and found that the transactions were closely spaced, with the final withdrawal taking place after a lunch break.
“Nag-lunch muna, tapos kinuha po ‘yun. Kaya sabi namin parang may hinahabol kasi right after lunch tuloy ‘yung transaction. Matagal din po kasi magbilang ng 41 million,” he said.

(They [Carpio's camp] had lunch first, then withdrew the money. That’s why we said it seemed like they were in a hurry because the transaction continued right after lunch. It also takes a long time to count P41 million.)
Sen. Kiko Pangilinan, meanwhile, questioned the timing of the withdrawals in relation to developments involving Duterte and Carpio.

"'Yung August 6, 2024, sabi ninyo 41 million ang winithdraw sa isang araw at parang may hinahabol. So ako rin naging curious dito, kaya iniisip ko, ano ba nangyari noong August 6 o kaya thereabouts, no?" Pangilinan said.

(On August 6, 2024, you said P41 million was withdrawn in a single day and that it seemed like someone was in a hurry. I became curious about this too so I wondered what happened on August 6 or around that time.)
He noted that Duterte resigned as education secretary on July 19, 2024, before drug charges were filed against Carpio on July 30 in connection with the so-called magnetic lifter case.

Just to place on record, uh, Vice President Sara Duterte resigned as DepEd chairperson July 19, 2024. And then on July 30, uh, it's in the news and we can Google it because that's what we did, uh, drug charges were filed against Attorney Mans Carpio doon sa, um, 'yong tawag dito, magnetic lifter," Pangilinan said.
"So July 30 'yun. So that was, uh, the filing was July 30, and then six days later nangyari ito," he added, referring to the August 6 withdrawals.
(So that was on July 30. The charges were filed on July 30, and then this happened six days later.)

Carpio has maintained that the credit card expenses discussed during the impeachment trial were personal expenditures paid for with his own money. He has also denied Duterte's involvement in the transactions and said no public funds were used.

Cabrera was presented by the prosecution as an expert witness on Article II of the impeachment complaint against Duterte, which accuses the vice president of amassing unexplained wealth disproportionate to her lawful income, failing to fully disclose her assets in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), and maintaining prohibited business interests while in office.

items: Actor RJ Mitte, known for his role as Walter White Jr. in 'Breaking Bad,' passed away at age 34 in Brownsville, Texas.
Mitte, who had cerebral palsy, used his personal experiences to bring authenticity to his roles and was an advocate for disability rights.
He was involved in philanthropic efforts for cerebral palsy awareness and also starred in the 2021 film 'Triumph' as a high school wrestler.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

LOS ANGELES, USA – Actor RJ Mitte, whose personal experience living with cerebral palsy informed his role as Walter White Jr, the physically disabled son of a methamphetamine kingpin in the landmark television show “Breaking Bad,” died on Monday, October 12, at age 34.

News of Mitte’s death in Brownsville, Texas, was confirmed in a statement released through the talent management agency that represented the actor. No other details about the circumstances of his death were given.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” the statement said.

Drawing from his real-life experience with cerebral palsy, Mitte was best known for his breakout role on the AMC cable TV series “Breaking Bad,” playing the only son of the lead character, Walter White, a terminally ill high school teacher who descends into a secret life of crime cooking crystal meth.

Mitte’s character, who adopted the nickname Flynn, used crutches and spoke with a slur, gains greater prominence as the story arc of the series progressed. He starts out as a carefree teenager who largely admires his father but later struggles to reckon with the family’s disintegration as the truth about Walter White’s “Heisenberg” alter ego emerges.

“Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion,” the statement said, noting that the actor was active in a number of philanthropic organizations devoted to fundraising and awareness for cerebral palsy and other muscle-control disorders.
The acclaimed series, often cited by critics as one of the best television dramas of all time, ran from 2008-2013, garnering 16 Emmy awards, including two for best drama series.

He later played a high school wrestler with cerebral palsy in the 2021 coming-of-age drama “Triumph.” He was a Screen Actors Guild spokesman for performers with disabilities, and a celebrity ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy. – Rappler.com

articles.title: 'Breaking Bad' actor and disability activist RJ Mitte dies
articles.summary: RJ Mitte said his lived experience with cerebral palsy was an asset for his role as Walter White's son Flynn on "Breaking Bad."

image.caption: RJ Mitte had key roles in 'Breaking Bad,' 'Switched at Birth' and 'Guardians of Justice'Image: Gage Skidmore/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: American actor RJ Mitte, whose lived experience with cerebral palsy was channeled into a key role in "Breaking Bad," died on Monday at the age of 34.
"It is with profound ​sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights ​advocate RJ Mitte," his management agency said in a statement.
No other details about the circumstances of his death were given.

In addition to his breakout role in in "Breaking Bad" and later credits including "Switched at Birth" and "Guardians of Justice," Mitte also served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Hospitals for Children.
An 'authentic' breakout role

In "Breaking Bad," Mitte played Walter White Jr., the son of Bryan Cranston's character, chemistry teacher-turned-meth dealer Walter White. Mitte's character used crutches and spoke with a slur, and gained greater prominence as the series progressed.
"Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built ​a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," the statement said.
"Breaking Bad" ran from 2008 until 2023. With 16 Emmy awards, it's often cited by critics as one of the best television dramas of all time.

Shortly after the series wrapped up, Mitte told the Associated Press that his disability and the surrounding struggles with physical therapy, family problems and exorbitant medical bills — all of which featured in the show — made him better in his role.
"You develop a different mentality and you develop a different look at how the world sees you and how you see the world," he said in 2024.
"You're able to use that. And I think it's an asset instead of something that would hinder," Mitte added.

articles.title: Pope Leo to enter hospital for surgery on lung nodule
articles.summary: The Vatican says the Pope's recovery is expected to take about a week. All his public events have been canceled until October 20.

blocks.text: THE POPE. Pope Leo XIV attends a meeting with university students and professors at the Catholic University of Central Africa in Yaounde, Cameroon, April 17, 2026.
REUTERS/Guglielmo Mangiapane
The Vatican says the Pope's recovery is expected to take about a week. All his public events have been canceled until October 20.

items: Pope Leo is scheduled for surgery on October 13 to remove a small growth on one of his lungs, marking his first major health issue since becoming pope 17 months ago.
The nodule was discovered during a checkup and is described as 'well-contained,' with a low risk of being cancerous according to medical experts.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
VATICAN – Pope Leo was due to be hospitalized in Rome on Tuesday, October 13, ahead of surgery to remove a small growth on one of his lungs, in the first major health issue of his 17-month tenure.
Leo, 71, said on Sunday, October 11, that a small nodule had been found on a checkup, was “well-contained” and had been spotted early.
He was expected to leave the Vatican for Rome’s Gemelli hospital late morning, the Vatican press office said, without specifying when the actual operation would take place.

Leo, elected by the world’s cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had health issues previously.
The Vatican has said his recovery is expected to take about a week. All his public events have been canceled until October 20.

A nodule on the lung is a small, localized lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking.

Dr. Federico Venuto, chief of thoracic surgery at Rome’s Policlinico Umberto I hospital, said procedures to remove lung nodules are usually minimally invasive, and can sometimes involve use of a thin camera tube called a thoracoscope.
“The complication rate is extremely low,” he told Reuters.
The late Pope Francis, Leo’s predecessor, died at age 88 in April 2025 and was hospitalized several times as he grew frail in his later years.
Leo, who spoke in a firm, clear voice at his only public event on Monday, keeps a very busy schedule. He is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17.
In the same address on Sunday when the pope announced his need for surgery, Leo pledged he would go forward with the trip. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Supreme Court orders release of mining tycoon Joseph Sy amid citizenship dispute
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered the release of Globe-Ferronickel chairman Joseph Sy.

blocks.text: October 13, 2026 | 8:22am
Joseph Sy attends the Senate inquiry on Dec. 15, 2025 which tackled the alleged abuse of identity documents reserved to Filipino citizens by foreign nationals.
Senate of the Philippines - Social Media Unit
MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court has ordered the release of Globe-Ferronickel chairman Joseph Sy.
In a resolution dated October 7, the high court granted a writ of preliminary mandatory injunction.
According to a copy of the order obtained by Philstar.com, the order took effect upon the posting of a P900,000.00 cash bond.
On Aug. 21, 2025, Sy was intercepted and detained by Bureau of Immigration personnel at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) upon his arrival from Hong Kong.

The bureau acted on a mission order issued by Immigration Commissioner Joel Viado, claiming that Sy was an alias for Zhong Zhen Chen, a Chinese national who had allegedly misrepresented himself as a Filipino.

To support their claim, immigration officials presented fingerprint evidence from an Alien Certificate of Registration issued 29 years ago, which they said matched the fingerprints on Sy's Philippine passport.
However, Sy’s representative, Dante Bravo, filed a petition for habeas corpus, arguing that Sy is a Filipino citizen.
Bravo provided Sy's Certificate of Live Birth, issued through late registration in 2007, which identifies him as a Filipino born in Quezon City to Filipino parents.
Sy also holds a Philippine passport valid until 2031 and various other government identification cards.

On February 20, the Court of Appeals ruled that Sy’s continued detention was unlawful, finding that the Bureau of Immigration cannot institute summary deportation proceedings against someone with a valid birth certificate.
In a statement, the Bureau of Immigration said that it would respect the Supreme Court’s decision.
However, the bureau emphasized that Sy's release from custody does not “constitute a final determination of the questions surrounding his citizenship and identity.”

“It is also noted that the case before the Supreme Court is an appeal in the Habeas Corpus Petition involving Mr. Sy, which only involves questions on legality of his detention, and not a determination on his citizenship,” the Bureau of Immigration’s statement read.
“The Bureau acted in the exercise of its statutory mandate to investigate questions concerning immigration status, identity, and citizenship documentation,” it added.

articles.title: Body found in stockyard trough confirmed to be missing 73-year-old Yvonne Whear
articles.summary: Whear was last seen on CCTV in mid-February buying orange juice and putting $50 credit on her phone in Murwillumbah

blocks.text: New South Wales police say a decomposed body found in a stockyard trough last week was missing woman Yvonne Whear, who vanished eight months ago after last being seen in Murwillumbah.
Last week, police said a partially submerged body believed to be a woman was discovered in a remote stockyard in Terragon near Murwillumbah.

The badly decomposed body was found partially submerged in a disused stock dip, a large trough commonly used to bathe livestock in anti-parasite solutions. Police on Tuesday confirmed it was Whear and her death was being treated as a homicide.
In mid-September, police divers found her car in the Rous River in Dulguigan – a short distance from her home.
“Several personal items, believed to belong to Yvonne, were also recovered,” police said at the time.

Whear was last seen on CCTV on 19 February buying orange juice and putting $50 credit on her phone at the Shell service station in Murwillumbah, before she drove through cane fields to her hobby farm at the hamlet of Dungay.
She had lived there for 23 years with a menagerie of animals she cared for.
At 8.30pm a member of the public reported seeing her car, a gold Ford Escape wagon, parked in the dark without lights, on Dungay Creek Road, less than a kilometre from where she lived.
Her daughter Gillian Hallac said that she never drove at night if she could help it.

blocks.caption: Gillian Hallac has been appealing for information after her mother, Yvonne Whear, who vanished earlier this year. Photograph: Supplied

blocks.text: Whear’s boots and hat that she had been wearing in the CCTV footage were still in her house, she had food in the slow cooker, her usual shoes were at the door. Her clothes were folded on her bed ready for the next day. Her family said she would never leave her animals.
Her phone last pinged at 10am the next day from a tower that put her mobile in the area where her car was subsequently found.
– More to come

articles.title: Shock and surprise after FBI arrests Canadian cybersecurity expert in ShinyHunters hacking case

image.caption: The FBI arrested a 'suspected co-conspirator' in the recent ShinyHunters cyberattack on FBIjobs.gov, who Reuters and court records have identified as Canadian cybersecurity expert Ed Dubrovsky. (Jenny Kane/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Canada
Canadians in the cybersecurity world say they were shocked to hear a prominent ransomware negotiator was arrested by the FBI over suspected connections to criminal hacking group ShinyHunters.
The prominent ransomware negotiator was arrested last week
· CBC News
· Posted: Oct 12, 2026 8:10 PM EDT | Last Updated: 21 minutes ago

Canadians in the cybersecurity world say they were shocked to hear that a prominent ransomware negotiator had been arrested by the FBI over suspected connections to criminal hacking group ShinyHunters.
FBI Director Kash Patel on Friday confirmed the arrest of a "suspected co-conspirator" in the recent ShinyHunters cyberattack on FBIjobs.gov which exposed a trove of sensitive data about FBI staff.
"We will continue to work closely with our partners to disrupt what's left of the ShinyHunters group and their associates, no matter where they operate," Patel said on social media.

Reuters reported Sunday that sources familiar with the matter identified the arrested suspect as Ed Dubrovsky, a Canadian cybersecurity executive whose career has focused on helping clients negotiate with ransomware attackers.

Court documents from the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania show Dubrovsky is facing two criminal charges: conspiracy to threaten to impair the confidentiality of information with the intent to extort money, and interference with commerce by threats.
The allegations have not been proven in court.

FBI Director Kash Patel testifies during a Senate Judiciary hearing on Oversight of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, in September 2026 in Washington. Patel confirmed the arrest of a suspected co-conspirator in the ShinyHunters investigation. (Manuel Balce Ceneta/The Associated Press)
'A sense of shock'
"For the cybersecurity community in general, I think that there's a sense of shock," Toronto-based tech and cybersecurity analyst Ritesh Kotak told CBC News on Monday.
Kotak says Dubrovsky is "very popular" and has spoken at numerous conferences, but stressed that the charges "are clearly just allegations" and that it is not yet known "what exactly has happened."
"This is an individual that was for the most part respected when it came to ransomware negotiations," he said. "A lot of people are familiar with his work as well."

items: ShinyHunters hackers say they won't leak sensitive FBI data
Dutch police arrest security professional in ShinyHunters investigation

blocks.text: The ​court records, which are partially sealed, provide conflicting spellings of the suspect's last ⁠name — "Dobrovsky" or "Dobrosky" — and do not identify his age, profession or employer.
Prison records show a 54-year-old named Edward Dubrovsky is being held at a federal detention centre in Philadelphia.

Reuters reported that electronic wallet records leaked in 2010 and preserved by dark-web intelligence firm District 4 Labs identify Dubrovsky as a 54-year-old resident of Richmond Hill, a suburb of Toronto.
Long history in cybersecurity

Dubrovsky's LinkedIn profile describes him as a specialist in ‌negotiating with cybercriminals over ransom payments, as well as a "globally recognized cybersecurity expert, business leader, speaker, author and educator."
According to his profile, Dubrovsky has held senior positions in cybersecurity for decades.

He wrote on LinkedIn last month that he would be attending the NetDilligence conference in Philadelphia in October with cybersecurity firm CyberSteward. The company posted photos of Dubrovsky at the conference a week ago and said he was signing copies of a book he recently published about handling cyber extortion.
AI can make cyberattacks faster and smarter

In the book's introduction, Dubrovsky writes: "I have negotiated with criminals who viewed themselves as martyrs, criminal masterminds, and patriots of their own countries even after deploying malware against critical infrastructure and causing billions of dollars in damage. Such people could still look in the mirror and see goodness."
CBC News reached out to CyberSteward by phone, email and in person at its Toronto address, but did not get a response Monday.
The FBI's national press office declined to comment directly on Dubrovsky's arrest and referred CBC News to Patel's statement.

RCMP spokesperson Ian Lordon told The Canadian Press on Friday that "the RCMP is aware of the arrest of a Canadian in the U.S. in connection with the ShinyHunters hack," but directed all further questions to the FBI.
ShinyHunters 'poked the bear': expert
ShinyHunters is known as one of the world's most prolific data theft and extortion groups, typically demanding ransom payments in exchange for not releasing the sensitive data it has obtained.

The hacking group caused chaos at universities around the world in May, including in Canada, with a cyberattack on Canvas, an online learning-management system that connects millions of students with their instructors.
ShinyHunters has also been associated with high-profile cyberattacks affecting companies including Telus, Microsoft, Ticketmaster, Pornhub and Rockstar Games.

items: What drives ShinyHunters, the group that claimed responsibility for hacking the FBI?

blocks.text: Last month, the group claimed responsibility for stealing a massive trove of data from the FBI — including officials' job assignments, addresses and social security numbers — in what it said was retaliation for the law enforcement agency making false claims about the group.
ShinyHunters later told CBC News they would not release the data.

David Shipley, a cybersecurity expert and CEO of Fredericton-based Beauceron Security, said the stunt "poked the bear" and has "literally unleashed the most powerful law enforcement agency in the world on them."
Online learning platform strikes deal with hackers that targeted schools | Hanomansing Tonight
Shipley said surprise was the first thing that came to mind when he heard of the latest arrest.
"I knew the ShinyHunters investigation was going to go in interesting places because it's already the stuff of Hollywood movies," he told CBC News.
"I don't think anyone saw this twist coming."
Shipley said Dubrovsky was well regarded and worked for "top-tier" cybersecurity firms.
"I feel terrible for his former colleagues, both at his current firm and his past firms, who have been dragged through these awful headlines," he said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Kevin Maimann is a senior writer for CBC News based in Edmonton. He has covered a wide range of topics for publications including VICE, the Toronto Star, Xtra Magazine and the Edmonton Journal. You can reach Kevin by email at kevin.maimann@cbc.ca.
With files from Reuters and The Canadian Press

articles.title: Scam or legit? Banks launch checker website, Google-backed game to learn
articles.summary: Even Google Philippines country manager Prep Palacios fell victim to a costly online scam: 'I'm a tech executive, and I was still fooled'

blocks.text: Even Google Philippines country manager Prep Palacios fell victim to a costly online scam: 'I'm a tech executive, and I was still fooled'

items: A new scam-checking website, ScamCheck.ph, allows users to assess suspicious messages and learn about common scams, developed by Metrobank and BetterGov.ph.
Banks and organizations are collaborating to enhance scam detection tools, while Google’s Be Scam Ready game helps users practice identifying scams through interactive scenarios.

Despite ongoing warnings, a significant percentage of Filipinos still fall victim to scams, with a report indicating that 84% encountered scams in the past year, leading to substantial financial losses.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – That urgent message asking you to transfer money for an emergency may look convincing, but before you open up your bank app, you can now use tools to get a second opinion or practice spotting scams.

A scam-checking website and an interactive game are among the tools being promoted as banks, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), and technology partners step up efforts to help Filipinos recognize fraud before sending money.

At ScamCheck.ph, users can paste suspicious text messages or upload screenshots for an AI-assisted assessment of whether they might be fraudulent. The website also provides information on common scams, allows victims to share their experiences, and offers guidance on reporting fraud.

The website was initially developed by Metrobank and civic technology group BetterGov.ph in late 2025, but is now being promoted more widely through the Bank Marketing Association of the Philippines’ (BMAP) campaign.

Jennifer Ng, BMAP director and program lead for the Scam Check Movement, said banks, government agencies, telecommunications companies, and other organizations are being encouraged to feed their legitimate messages, promotional materials, and communications to train the tool in better distinguishing authentic messages from those impersonating banks and government offices.

For those who want to practice, Google’s Be Scam Ready game puts players through scenarios based on scam tactics. Players follow a character’s story, making decisions and getting feedback on their ability to detect scams.

blocks.caption: Stay alert online: Join anti-scam community forum in Laguna

blocks.text: The initiatives come as regulators acknowledge that repeatedly warning Filipinos about scams has done little to stop people from falling victim.

“We keep coming up with the same messages over and over again and yet people are still scammed,” BSP Deputy Governor Bernadette Romulo-Puyat told reporters on Monday, October 12. “It’s not enough to come up with social media [posts that say] don’t share personal information, don’t press on links.”
She said the BSP is working with BMAP and behavioral science specialists to improve how scam warnings are communicated, with the goal of getting consumers to act on them before making transactions.
Even Google Philippines country manager Prep Palacios knows how easily someone can fall for a scam.

A couple of years ago, she was making an online purchase and had what seemed like a professional exchange with the seller. But after she sent her payment, the seller’s account disappeared, along with their messages. She lost P90,000.
“It wasn’t really just about the money. It was the realization of how easily I got manipulated,” Palacios said. “I’m a tech executive, and I was still fooled.”
A 2026 report by the Global Anti-Scam Alliance (GASA) found that 84% of Filipino adults surveyed encountered a scam attempt in the past year.

Some 15% reported losing money directly or through stolen personal information that resulted in financial losses, even as more than half of the respondents expressed confidence in their ability to recognize scams.
The study, based on a survey of 1,160 adults, estimated that Filipinos lost P121.8 billion to scams annually, averaging P10,427 per victim.

Meanwhile, Google.org, Google’s philanthropic arm, has committed $5 million to the ASEAN Foundation’s Scam Ready ASEAN program, which runs from 2025 to 2027. The funding covers regional scam-prevention activities, including interactive learning tools and the training of 2,000 master trainers who are expected to educate at least 550,000 people across Southeast Asia.
Locally, BMAP programs director Catherine “Peewee” Villanueva said the training effort aims to reach one million Filipinos through schools and communities.

An initial 105 master trainers, mostly from banks and other financial institutions, have been mobilized. They will train others within their organizations, while banks plan to incorporate scam prevention into existing financial literacy programs. – Rappler.com

articles.title: LIST: The Marcos administration’s cybersecurity efforts
articles.summary: The Marcos administration details its initiatives aimed to be completed by 2028 under the second National Cybersecurity Plan

blocks.text: The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s administration developed the second iteration of the National Cybersecurity Plan (NCSP).
This plan aims to address the country’s growing vulnerability to cyber threats and achieve the following outcomes by the end of Marcos’ term in 2028:

items: Proactive protection and security of national cyberspace
Increased workforce capability
Strengthened policy framework

blocks.text: According to the DICT, the plan aligns with the country’s Development Plan, National Security Strategy, National Cybercrime Strategy, and other cybersecurity strategies by national government agencies. On April 6, 2024, Marcos officially gave the green light to carry out the plan and adopted it through Executive Order No. 58.
Below are the government efforts listed under the NCSP.

1. National Fiber Backbone (NFB): A high-speed, government-owned nationwide broadband network. This allows the recalibration of Government Network (GovNet) infrastructure security and unites all national and local government agencies into one Wide Area Network (WAN).
The initiative began rolling out its initial phase in 2023 and launched Phase 1 of the Mindanao Integrated Government Network last June.

2. National government cloud platform: It will be used for storing confidential government data in close coordination with the Department of National Defense (DND), Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), and Philippine National Police (PNP) to secure the physical internetwork of GovNet and the NFB. It also includes the landing stations and submarine cable systems.
The DICT kickstarted its Cloud First Policy in 2017 and has built on it ever since. In 2024, the e-GovCloud initiative hosted 1,277 government systems.

3. Strengthened National Computer Emergency Response Team (NCERT) and Modernized National Security Operations Center (NSOC): On April 7, 60 more agencies were onboarded as part of the national plan. This expands the operation’s coverage nationwide.

These teams would handle incident response, investigation, government Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) services, threat monitoring and hunting, malware analysis, and threat advisories. A centralized system accessible by other agencies would also be in place to delegate incident tickets for monitoring.

4. National cybersecurity threat database: An accessible database that categorizes threats and is uploadable to cybersecurity defense systems. In 2024, the DICT said NSOC monitors over two million cyber threats per day. However, as of writing, the database is not yet publicly accessible.

5. Partnerships with Public Telecommunication Entities (PTEs) and Internet Service Providers (ISPs): The DICT, National Telecommunications Commission (NTC), and telecom providers would establish reporting protocols to assist in security countermeasures to detect threats and malicious activities early and combat malware outbreaks.

Major telecommunications companies, such as Globe Telecom, Smart Communications, PLDT, Converge ICT Solutions Incorporated, Infinivan, and PT&T, have begun their partnership with the DICT in 2025. This laid the groundwork for the nationwide rollout of the Protective Domain Name System (PDNS), which scans DNS queries in real time and blocks access to dangerous websites, including those used for phishing, malware, and the spread of fake news.

6. Misinformation combat: On April 14, the DICT partnered with the Presidential Communications Office and the Department of Justice to launch “Oplan Kontra Fake News,” an inter-agency framework designed to curb the spread of disinformation and AI-generated deepfakes.

7. National Cybersecurity Intelligence Fusion Center: The plan looks to establish a nationwide network of CERTs with clearly defined roles and a new incident response model. The NCSP detailed a new workflow and hierarchical model, with the DICT NCERT and the Defense CERT as top command.
As of July, the DICT partnered with the Korea International Cooperation Agency to build a physical cybersecurity center in Valenzuela.

8. Securing submarine cable infrastructure: The DICT will coordinate with government agencies such as the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) to develop a map of all cables and them to prevent damage due to theft, anchorage, earthquakes, and major climate disturbances.

Earlier this year, the DICT partnered with Australia’s Cable Connectivity and Resilience Centre to develop a framework to protect the country’s subsea cables and submitted the analysis to Marcos. Telco companies PLDT, Globe, and Converge also joined the agency to plan a cable system that will loop around the country, which may be completed in 24 months.

9. Bilateral and multilateral international cooperation: The plan looks to expand existing agreements with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, the United Nations, Interpol, and other bilateral agreements with other countries.

The country has partnered with Korea to build a cybersecurity center. It also had a Cyber-Digital Policy dialogue with the United States in 2024 to strengthen both countries’ ICT, their resilience to cybersecurity threats, and the growth of the digital economy.

1. October as Cybersecurity Awareness Month: On October 2, 2023, Marcos signed Proclamation No. 353, changing the commemoration of Cybersecurity Awareness Month from September to October. This coincides with the international cybersecurity month celebrations.

2. ICT Academy: The ICT Literacy and Competency Development Bureau (ILCDB) was upgraded to ICT Academy on October 1 to develop a highly skilled workforce capable of addressing cybersecurity challenges. It would also engage with research initiatives and collaborate with industry partners, government agencies, and international bodies to ensure a globally accepted approach.

3. Cybersecurity jobs in government: The DICT would collaborate with the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and the Civil Service Commission (CSC) to create official job titles, hiring qualifications, and specialized exams for cybersecurity career service positions in the government.

Under the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act No. 12254, signed on March 24, the three agencies were required to develop guidelines establishing specialized cybersecurity positions across all national agencies, including local governments, state universities and colleges (SUCs), and government-owned or controlled corporations.

4. Partnerships with local and international training providers: The department would work with private industry leaders to create online short courses that would be internationally recognized and certified.

It has already secured a multi-year deal with Google to enhance the country’s cybersecurity defense. The partnership would train public servants to use Gemini Enterprise and Google Workspace, with the end goal of training 200,000 people nationwide over the next 18 months.

5. Cybersecurity programs and scholarships: The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and SUCs are encouraged to develop cybersecurity degree programs. The DICT would also partner with TESDA in creating National Certification in various cybersecurity skills. These programs would also be included in partial and full scholarships.

In 2019, CHED has already listed cybersecurity as one of the priority courses for scholarship programs under Memorandum Order No. 5, s. 2019. As of writing, some universities offer cybersecurity programs, including Mapúa University, De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde, and Lyceum of the Philippines University.

6. National and international hacking competitions: The DICT would organize regional and national hacking competitions where winners would take part in international competitions. The agency would also build a network of experts, resource persons, and trainers.

The DICT kicked off HackForGov in 2019, an annual nationwide cybersecurity competition. It has become an annual competition since then, with different regions hosting the event. Winners would eventually represent the country in the annual Cyber SEA Game.

1. Strengthening National Cybersecurity Inter-Agency Committee: Marcos has reinforced the established committee, created under E.O. 189, s. 2015. The committee would serve as a convergence hub of different government agencies and the main forum for information sharing, planning, and ensuring policies don’t conflict with other interests.
The President has then mandated the DICT to submit biannual implementation reports on national cyber policies.

2. Executive Order on Critical Infrastructure and Critical Information Infrastructure: E.O. 119, s. 2026 updated government data classification, and the framework for data security. This covers all digital or hybrid government-owned data, including private service providers that handle government data.
3. Mandatory security labelling of devices: The plan looks to require routers and switches sold in the market to be labeled to inform the public about the security of the products.

4. Revision on VAPT service providers’ accreditation: The DICT revised the existing accreditation of VAPT service providers last January under Department Circular No. HRA-001, s. 2026. The revisions would add customer feedback through complaint mechanisms and train service providers on managing them.

5. Establish policies, guidelines, and procedures on network security systems: The DICT would partner with the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Department of Science and Technology, the academe, and industry partners to develop network security system protocols.

The agency has already released Department Circular No. 003, s. 2024, mandating all government agencies to adhere to security measures and response protocols. This also includes rerouting internet traffic to DICT-managed PDNS, automated vulnerability scans, and sharing information with the NSOC.

6. Minimum cybersecurity standards: Under Republic Act NO. 12254, the DICT was prescribed to implement minimum information security standards for government systems. In March 2026, an IRR was issued requiring all government agencies to comply.

7. Legislative Agenda and Enactments: The DICT would endorse key legislative measures to Congress to resolve economic challenges, information asymmetry, and establish legal cybersecurity protections. In 2026, the House of Representatives approved on third and final reading House Bill No. 9605, or the proposed “National Cybersecurity and Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Act of 2026.”

The bill is aligned with the administration’s Digital Transformation Framework and seeks to establish mandatory cybersecurity standards and certification systems, ensuring consistent defense protocols for public and private sectors. – Rappler.com

articles.title: One dead and more injured after incident on Six Flags rollercoaster in US
articles.summary:
Six Flags Over Georgia ‘deeply saddened’ by tragedy, reportedly occurring on Goliath coaster with 175ft drop

One person has died and several others were injured in an incident involving a…

blocks.text: One person has died and several others were injured in an incident involving a Six Flags rollercoaster on Monday afternoon in Georgia, according to police.
The incident took place a Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (25km) north-west of Atlanta, according to the Cobb county police department.

Officials did not confirm how the person died or what caused the others to be injured. However, multiple outlets reported a person had fallen from the park’s Goliath rollercoaster, citing eyewitnesses and anonymous local officials.
The rollercoaster, which was introduced at the park in 2006, has a top speed of 70mph (110km/h) and a 175ft drop.
A Six Flags spokesperson said the park and local authorities responded immediately and that they are fully cooperating with local authorities as they investigate the incident.
“We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today,” the spokesperson said.

Late last month, Six Flags Magic Mountain, in southern California, announced that it was retiring its famous X2 rollercoaster amid lawsuits alleging serious brain injury caused by the ride. Six Flags recently settled a wrongful-death lawsuit from the family of a 22-year-old man who died after riding the coaster in 2022, and three more lawsuits alleging traumatic brain injuries were filed last week.

articles.title: English councils warn of ‘catastrophic’ Send debts forecast to hit £10bn by 2028
articles.summary:
Surge in EHCP applications poses risk to public finances and may lead to deteriorating levels of support

Councils are warning of potentially “catastrophic” debts, which are forecast to reach…

blocks.text: Councils are warning of potentially “catastrophic” debts, which are forecast to reach a record £10bn over the next 18 months, as a result of rapid growth in demand for special educational needs and disability (Send) support in English schools.

Although the government recently cleared more than £5bn in historic council Send debts, a surge in requests has led to authorities predicting they will have re-accrued that debt figure by April, and doubled it by 2028.

The recent acceleration in applications for education, health and care plans (EHCPs), which mandate support for conditions such as speech and learning difficulties, autism or ADHD, is thought to partly reflect a rush by parents and schools to secure support before the government’s changes to Send provision take effect.

The prospect of council finances being overwhelmed by schools’ Send spending reflects similar concerns in the NHS and the benefit system over the strain the rising prevalence of mental health and neurodevelopmental conditions has put on public services.

The government-commissioned Fonagy report, published last week, found the increase in these conditions was real and a cause of distress to many who have them, but the resulting demand for support would be unsustainable without introducing new ways to manage the pressure on public services.

The County Councils Network (CCN), which published the forecasts on Tuesday, said the overspending was not the fault of councils and called on ministers to guarantee future Send debts run up by local authorities, some of whom would be otherwise left effectively bankrupt as a result of meeting their legal duties.

Linden Kemkaran, the CCN’s Send spokesperson, said: “These deficits have not accumulated because councils have chosen to spend recklessly: they are the result of having to meet rapidly growing statutory demand, which has only intensified this year, without funding keeping pace.

“If councils are left carrying billions of pounds of Send debt, it will not just be a problem for local authorities. Taxpayers and local communities will ultimately bear the consequences as councils face impossible choices about how to protect frontline services while managing debts that have accrued through no fault of their own.

She added: “As well as councils absorbing skyrocketing costs, children and young people will face increasingly long waits for support and educational outcomes will continue to flatline. New ministers now need to provide certainty that they will deliver the full package of reforms needed to ensure the system works much better for young people, schools and councils.”

The government’s reforms aim to gradually replace the current system in England with a more inclusive approach of Send support in mainstream schools that in principle obviates the need for an EHCP. However, parents appear to be rushing to secure formal support now to avoid any future uncertainty.

Without a ministerial guarantee to wipe future overspending, councils say they are at risk of bankruptcy when those accumulated debts – currently kept off town hall balance sheets under a special “override” arrangement with the Treasury – go back on to the books in April 2028 when the override is due to expire.

Ministers have agreed to pay 90% of English top tier councils’ Send debts accumulated to March 2026, but it is unclear how far future Send debts will be covered. Ministers have previously said future debt support would be “appropriate and proportionate” but that it would “not be unlimited”.

The CCN said anything less than a ministerial commitment to pay down 90% of future Send debt would be a “financial catastrophe” for councils – and some authorities would struggle with solvency even if they retained just 10% of their Send debts.

Publicly available internal reports by local authorities show a number are predicting overspends of more than £100m in 2026-27 alone. Hampshire county council is forecasting a £200m deficit for this year. Others include Surrey, East Sussex, Kent, Worcestershire and Norfolk county councils.

The EHCPs are legal documents agreed between local authorities and families in England detailing the support required for children and young people up to the age of 25, allowing access to extra funding or places in special schools.

In January, the number of young people with EHCPs reached 718,000, after a 12.5% increase over the past 12 months. This was the largest year on year increase since the plans were introduced in 2014. An additional 1.3 million young people have identified special needs, according to official data.

Many councils are anticipating annual double digit increases over the next three years, with several now projecting that at the current rates of increase, nearly one in 10 pupils will have an EHCP by 2029.

The Fonagy report said the growth in EHCPs had “substantially outpaced the capacity” of the education system to respond. Of the 105,300 statutory assessments carried out in 2024, 94% resulted in the award of an EHCP.

Owen Mapley, the chief executive of the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy, said: “The continued escalation of Send deficits exposes a serious failure to align statutory responsibilities with funding levels. Local government chief financial officers have been calling attention to this disconnect for years as it undermines proper financial management practice.”

A government spokesperson said: “We inherited a Send system under immense strain, and have always recognised that both deficits and EHCP applications will continue to rise before our reforms are fully rolled out.

“On top of grants to pay off 90% of council deficits, we’re investing billions to make sure every community has easy, early access to specialists like speech and language therapists, and so councils can deliver their tailored local reform plans.
“Fixing the Send system will take time and councils will need further support with deficits, so we will set out the details before March 2028.”

articles.title: Queensland ombudsman backs away from calls to close youth prison so ‘unsuitable’ some children self-harm to get transferred
articles.summary: Inmate advocacy group attacks watchdog’s ‘gutless retreat’ on Wacol youth remand centre

blocks.text: The Queensland ombudsman has backed away from calls to close a youth prison so “unsuitable” for children that some are self-harming in an attempt to get transferred, amid concerns that the Crisafulli government’s hardline bail laws could create a new crowding crisis in police watch houses.

The ombudsman, Anthony Reilly, published an inspection report last week that raised serious new concerns about the suitability of the Wacol youth remand centre to hold children for extended periods, including the fact that young people were being held in conditions where there is “a lack of space, privacy and natural light”.
The facility, near Brisbane, is often used to hold Indigenous children from north Queensland due to overcrowding at the Cleveland youth detention centre in Townsville.

The report found that some children stayed for longer than a month and that some “complex and high risk” children were shifted back to the remand centre after being placed in a youth detention centre.

Staff told inspectors that some children from north Queensland who had spent extended time at the centre “displayed negative behaviours and engaged in acts of self‑harm to influence and expedite their transfer to another centre”.
The Wacol centre was built and designed as a police watch house but was converted under law to a youth detention centre.

The operation of the Wacol centre has in some ways eased pressure on police watch houses, and the practice of holding vulnerable children in crowded police cells – in some cases for more than 30 days – due to a lack of available places in youth detention. Data shows fewer children held in watch houses, and for shorter periods.
Critics and children’s advocates say the government has simply shifted the problem to Wacol.

Queensland is building a new youth detention centre at Woodford and Reilly had previously called for the Wacol facility – which he says is “austere and institutional” and unsuitable to hold children for long periods – to be closed when the new facility is opened.

But the ombudsman has backed away from that recommendation in his latest report, over concerns that new state bail laws – dubbed “breach bail, go to jail” – could cause the population of young people in prison to explode, triggering a new crisis in watch houses.

“In the year ahead, it may be the case that the impacts of the above reforms are such that the existing three youth detention centres and the new Woodford youth detention centre do not have sufficient capacity to accommodate the number of children that our criminal justice system requires to be detained,” Reilly said in his report.
after newsletter promotion

“As a consequence, it is possible that children will need to be detained in large numbers and for lengthy periods in watch-houses. In this scenario, it would be beneficial for the Wacol [centre] to continue to be available to accommodate children to minimise the number of children detained in watch‑houses, and the length of their stay.
“While we do not consider the centre to be a suitable facility for the detention of children, we consider it to be more suitable than detention in police watch-houses.”

Sisters Inside, an organisation that supports women and girls in custody, described the backdown as “a gutless retreat” that “allows the government’s determination to imprison more children to dictate what an independent watchdog is prepared to tolerate”.

“The ombudsman has identified that Wacol is unsuitable for children, then backed away from demanding its closure because the government intends to lock up even more of them,” said Debbie Kilroy, Sisters Inside’s chief executive.
“If a facility is unsuitable for children, it does not become suitable because the government creates something worse. Children’s safety cannot be negotiated down to accommodate a political agenda.”
Kilroy said the findings demanded “a clear stand for children’s safety”.

articles.title: 2 Filipinos under probe over Laos shabu haul bound for PH — PDEA
articles.summary: The agency said they are currently building a case against the two Filipinos, noting that some of the information remains confidential amid the probe.

blocks.text: October 13, 2026 | 6:54am
Motorists drive past Laos national flags and Lao People's Revolutionary Party flags ahead of the election in Vientiane on February 19, 2026.
STR / AFP

MANILA, Philippines — Two Filipinos are currently the subjects of an ongoing investigation by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) over their alleged link to a recent high-value drug bust in Laos, which authorities also confirmed was bound for the Philippines.

In a press briefing on Monday, October 12, the drug enforcement agency said they have established that the 521 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine, or shabu, that Lao authorities intercepted over a week ago at Luang Prabang International Airport was supposed to be delivered to the Philippines through a private jet.

The pilot of the private jet reportedly refused to load the luggage of the Filipino passenger who was carrying the luggage, which eventually led to the individual’s arrest and the plane’s cancellation of its flight to the Philippines.

“The very clear feature as of today is na-discover iyong droga dahil the pilot refused to load those baggages doon sa airplane papuntang Pilipinas. Kaya nung hindi na natuloy ‘yung ah 'yung pag-load ng baggages doon sa eroplano, ang ginawa ng airline company canceled its flight plan papunta sa Pilipinas,” PDEA Director General Undersecretary Isagani Nerez said.

(The very clear feature as of today is that the drugs were discovered because the pilot refused to load those baggages in the airplane bound for the Philippines. That's why the loading of baggage did not proceed, and the airline company canceled its flight going to the Philippines.)
The agency identified the arrested suspect as “Fajad”, a confirmed Filipino national with alleged current residence in Marawi. Nerez said they also have a list of Fajad’s other addresses.
Authorities are now investigating to identify Fajad’s accomplices while he remains detained in Laos, including another Filipino identified as “Boyet”.
'Boyet'
Nerez said Boyet is among the persons of interest in PDEA’s target list for allegedly being responsible for chartering the private jet that was supposed to be used to transport the suspected drugs.
The authorities said they have established a link between Fajad and Boyet, and found that both of them have residences in Luzon.
“We have a data that si Boyet is taga-rito sa Luzon, at ‘yung si Fajad meron ding address sa Luzon, parehas po. So that links them na or establish 'yung link nila na magkakilala,” Nerez said.
(We have data showing that Boyet is from Luzon, and Fajad also has an address in Luzon. So that links them or establishes a connection between them, suggesting that they know each other.)
Boyet allegedly paid for the private jet through bank transfer, but authorities did not disclose the amount.
PDEA also said they have acquired information saying Boyet had already skipped the country and went to Hong Kong.
The agency said they are currently building a case against both Boyet and Fajad, noting that some of the information remains confidential amid the probe.

Day 38 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Oct. 12, 2026. Senate
Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 39: What to expect
The Senate impeachment court on Tuesday is set to tackle the manifestation of the House prosecution panel to drop Article III or the bribery charges in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Presiding officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero acknowledged on Monday the receipt of the October 6 manifestation by the prosecution, saying that the impeachment court is taking the matter “in advisement.”

“[The trial shall] resume tomorrow for the final manifestations to be made by the panel of prosecutors, as well as any other manifestations the parties wish to make, as well as administrative matters that the court need to address, if indeed the panel of prosecutors will persist in their intention to drop Article III and to rest all together,” Escudero said during the trial on Monday.
The impeachment court is set to resume the trial at 1 p.m. today.
The House prosecution has already presented three out of the four Articles of Impeachment originally filed against Duterte.

The first was Article IV or the alleged grave threats against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez.
This was followed by Article I or the alleged misuse of confidential funds.
The prosecution on Monday finished with the presentation of evidence for Article II, pertaining to the allegation that the Vice President amassed millions in unexplained wealth.
The last witness the prosecution presented for its case-in-chief was financial forensic analyst Atty. Alexander Cabrera.

Should the prosecution rest its case today, it will be given time by the court to submit its formal offer of evidence in the impeachment trial. The defense is expected to comment on the matter. —Giselle Ombay/BAP/KG, GMA News

articles.title: Canada falls 4-3 to Denmark in women's soccer friendly in Toronto
articles.summary: Olivia Holdt scored twice and had an assist to lead Denmark to a 4-3 victory over Canada in a women's international soccer friendly on Monday at BMO Field in Toronto.

image.caption: Canada goalkeeper Kailen Sheridan, left, and teammate Janine Sonis react after Denmark's Olivia Holdt, not shown, scored her country's third goal during first half of Monday's international friendly at BMO Field in Toronto. (Chris Young/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Soccer·New
Olivia Holdt scored twice and had an assist to lead Denmark to a 4-3 victory over Canada in a women's international soccer friendly on Monday at BMO Field in Toronto.
The teams played to a 1-1 draw on Friday in Montreal
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Oct 12, 2026 6:17 PM EDT | Last Updated: 12 minutes ago
Pernille Harder and Janni Thomsen also tallied for the visitors, who blitzed the hosts with three goals in a nine-minute span in the opening half.
Olivia Smith, Evelyne Viens and Delaney Pridham scored for Canada in front of an announced crowd of 12,112 on a warm, mostly sunny afternoon at the lakefront stadium.
The teams played to a 1-1 draw on Friday in Montreal. Smith scored a late equalizer for the hosts in that game and Canada won the unofficial shootout 4-2.

On Monday, the ninth-ranked Canadians started with a 4-2-3-1 formation while the 12th-ranked Danes went with a 3-4-3. Kailen Sheridan started in net for Canada and Jessie Fleming wore the captain's armband.
Canada comes up just short against Denmark in Toronto FIFA friendly

Pridham opened the scoring in the 10th minute after Kaylee Hunter headed the ball low into a packed penalty area. Pridham swiveled and beat goalkeeper Freja Thisgaard for her first goal with the women's senior team.
Canada kept the pressure on and was nearly rewarded moments later when Smith's shot from outside the area glanced off Thisgaard and hit the post.
Denmark scoring surge
Defensive miscues contributed to the Denmark scoring surge.

Holdt took possession of a loose ball after Canada's Julia Grosso couldn't corral a pass from defender Kadeisha Buchanan at midfield. The Danish forward took a few strides inside the halfway line and launched a shot that sailed over Sheridan's head and bounced into the net in the 24th minute.

An errant pass attempt by Buchanan moments later created another turnover. A strike from Sofie Bredgaard hit the crossbar but Denmark controlled the rebound and Harder beat Sheridan in the 27th minute.
In the 32nd minute, Ashley Lawrence's pass to Jade Rose was turned over down low and the ball found its way to an open Holdt, who earned her first international brace.
The tempo picked up in the second half as Pridham and Buchanan came off for Viens and Shelina Zadorsky.

Canada cut the deficit in the 49th minute after some heady work by Smith, who found Viens at the top of the area. Viens made a sliding shot attempt that deflected high off a defender and bounced off the grass and into the top corner.
Thomsen restored Denmark's two-goal cushion in the 61st minute as she coolly slotted a ball between two defenders and past Sheridan.
Smith scored from outside the box in the 70th minute. Her strike was misplayed by Thisgaard, who got down low to gather the ball but had it roll between her legs and over the line.
Casey Stoney is still seeking her first victory against a top-15 opponent since taking over as Canada's head coach in January 2025.
Upcoming CONCACAF W Championship
The friendlies served as a measuring stick ahead of Canada's opening match against No. 54 Panama at the CONCACAF W Championship on Nov. 28.

The tournament is a qualifier for both the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Denmark has already qualified for the World Cup after finishing atop its UEFA qualifying group.
Left back Allysha Chapman came on in the 89th minute for her 100th and final international appearance for Canada. She was feted during a ceremony after the game.

Fleming, Buchanan and Lawrence were honoured before the game for reaching 150 career international appearances. At halftime, Melissa Tancredi was acknowledged for her induction into the Canada Soccer Hall of Fame.
Canada fell to 3-4-1 in eight all-time meetings against Denmark.

articles.title: Emergency medical help for Christa Pike was delayed due to confusion, 911 tapes reveal
articles.summary: Emergency help for Christa Pike was delayed by confusion among first responders and Tennessee prison officials following her failed lethal injection last month, according to 911 dispatch recordings…

image.caption: 911 recordings suggest emergency care was delayed after the failed execution of Christa Pike, seen here in December 2007. (J. Miles Cary/ Knoxville News Sentinel/USA Today Network/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Emergency help for Christa Pike was delayed by confusion among first responders and Tennessee prison officials following her failed lethal injection last month, according to 911 dispatch recordings reviewed by The Associated Press.
First responders not sure whether request for emergency help in execution chamber was legitimate

The recordings show that precious minutes elapsed as officials and responders tried to figure out whether a request for emergency help in the execution chamber was legitimate. The first call came in at 8:40 p.m. local time on Sept. 30, and it was about half an hour before prison officials affirmed it was legitimate and began letting responders through the prison gates.

"Per supervisors here at the DEC [Department of Emergency Communications], we have been informed it is a false call," one unidentified person says at 9:03 p.m. "There is no medical assistance needed at Riverbend Prison."

items: Tennessee governor orders outside review after death row inmate Christa Pike survives execution attempt
After day of delays, witnesses say Tennessee unable to carry out execution of Christa Pike

blocks.text: Four minutes later, a responder reported: "Somebody is outside the gate at the prison telling us that it's real and demanding us to go in. They say they are some sort of state official. I need somebody to get out to the gate and talk to those people."
It wasn't until 9:11 p.m. that prison officials affirmed the call for help was legitimate, the calls show.
Pike discharged from hospital

Pike, 50, was hospitalized after surviving two doses of pentobarbital as the state attempted to execute her for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. At one point, Pike was on a ventilator, and her lawyers did not expect her to survive.

However, they said Pike woke up and began talking and walking with assistance, and she has since been discharged and is back at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, the women's prison where she was housed for 30 years.

The Tennessee Department of Correction has not said what went wrong in the attempted execution. Medical and lethal injection experts have focused on whether a problem with the IV line caused the drug to pool in her tissue instead of entering her bloodstream.

articles.title: Cyberattack defrosts French supermarket freezers, spoiling food at 100s of stores
articles.summary: Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50 C overnight, causing fires ‌and spoiling food.

image.caption: A woman walks past empty frozen-food refrigerators at an Intermarché supermarket in Névez, France, on Monday, following a cyberattack affecting the French supermarket chains. (Fred Tanneau/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New
Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50 C overnight, causing fires ‌and spoiling food.
Freezer temperatures were remotely raised to as high as 50 C at stores across France
The Paris prosecutor's office said on Monday that a "large-scale" attack was "affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France," leading to food losses and fires.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has instructed France's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) to investigate, a person in his office said.

France was co-ordinating with European counterparts because other countries could also be affected, the person said, adding that authorities were assessing whether other French companies were at risk.
Félix Aimé, a senior ​cyber threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia Threat Detection and Research, said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium ​had also been affected.
Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets were hit, while Monoprix, which operates about 490 stores in France, said five per cent of its stores were affected.

A frozen food aisle at a supermarket near Nantes, closed after a cyberattack targeted refrigeration systems at French supermarket chains, causing food losses and fires at several stores. (Stephane Mahe/Reuters)
All affected food thrown out

Les Mousquetaires, owner of retailer Intermarché, said fridges at around 150 of its stores were heated up to 50 ​C for six hours overnight. A spokesperson said all affected food had been discarded to eliminate health risks.

Paris resident Geert de Clercq ⁠witnessed staff at an Intermarché in central Paris ⁠throwing cartfuls of defrosted frozen foods into a giant trash container, with molten ice ‌cream sloshing out of broken tubs on the street.
Coopérative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said his supermarket group had also been targeted.
"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," he wrote on X.
Food retailers E.Leclerc and Auchan did not respond to requests for comment.

There was no immediate estimate of industry-wide losses, but Intermarché CEO Thierry Cotillard told BFM TV ⁠the "unprecedented" attack would represent losses amounting to "tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day."
Christel Delberghe, director general at European retail association Eurocommerce, said, "This incident underlines the importance of resilience across the entire supply chain."
AI can make cyberattacks faster and smarter
Control panels accessible over internet

Supermarket cold aisles are typically run by control panels that manage an entire store's fridges and freezers and can be accessed over ‌the internet, which lets maintenance companies adjust them from anywhere.
The source close to Lecornu said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.
Danfoss said it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems."

The affected units "were running outdated firmware," Danfoss said, adding that it had "long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions."
Want to protect yourself from today’s cybersecurity and AI threats? Here are a few tips

On Aug. 9, cybersecurity firm ​Claroty's Team82 published research detailing vulnerabilities in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller. According to the report, software updates issued by Danfoss addressed issues that could have allowed attackers to bypass authentication controls and execute code on compromised devices.
The attacks resemble disruptions ⁠reported at about a dozen U.S. military commissaries in late August that led to food losses after fridges were affected.
Dutch security issue

Dutch ​retailer Ahold Delhaize, which operates the Netherlands's largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn and has major operations in the U.S., said it was dealing with a "security issue" on its network and ​had taken several systems offline as a precaution.
A message ⁠on the retailer's smartphone app said it was unable to deliver groceries because of a "cybersecurity incident."
Online orders account for about 10 per cent of Albert Heijn sales. Physical stores remained open, while Dutch news agency ANP reported that rival retailers had seen a surge in delivery orders.
Ahold Delhaize said there was no reason to see a link between the incidents in France and its supermarkets.
Ahold is the fourth-largest grocery retailer in the U.S. Websites for its Stop & Shop, Giant, Hannaford and Food Lion chains displayed notices saying "site temporarily down."
It was unclear whether other operations had been ⁠affected.

articles.title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
articles.summary: The actor, who played the defiant son of drug kingpin Walter White in the drama series, dies aged 34.

blocks.text: US actor RJ Mitte, best known for his role as the defiant son of drug kingpin Walter White in the drama series Breaking Bad, has died aged 34.
"It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," his representative told the BBC.
He died in Brownsville, Texas. No immediate cause of death was provided.

Mitte, who lived with cerebral palsy, drew on his own experience for his role as Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series starring Bryan Cranston and Aaron Paul. He earned a Screen Actors Guild Award in 2014 for his work on the series.
"Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," his representative Sean Reilly said in a statement to the BBC.
Mitte also served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children's.

He created The Mitte Foundation as well, to support philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, using his platform "to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities", Reilly said.
Breaking Bad aired on US cable broadcaster AMC for five seasons from 2008 to 2013.

The anti-hero drama created by Vince Gilligan earned a whopping 58 Primetime Emmy nominations and won 16, including two for Outstanding Drama Series in 2013 and 2014. It is widely credited as being one of the best US TV series of the 21st century.

Cranston plays a high school chemistry teacher in New Mexico who turns to a life of crime to support his family after a cancer diagnosis. As he descends deeper into the underbelly of the meth trade, he drifts further from his son, Walt Jr, who made his displeasure known with levity through much of the series.

articles.title: Bolivia investigates ex-president Evo Morales over alleged ties to 2009 killings
articles.summary:
Leftist former leader accused of involvement in shooting of three Europeans in Santa Cruz and torture of two others

Bolivia’s attorney general has announced an investigation into leftist…

blocks.text: Bolivia’s attorney general has announced an investigation into leftist former president Evo Morales, alleging his involvement in the murder and torture of European citizens in 2009.
Seventeen years ago, police raided a hotel in the city of Santa Cruz, shooting dead Eduardo Rózsa Flores, a Bolivian-Croatian, Michael Dwyer, an Irishman, and Árpád Magyarosi, a Hungarian-Romanian.
Bolivian-Croatian citizen Mario Tadic and Elöd Tóásó from Hungary survived and reported being tortured after their arrest.
The Morales administration in power at the time claimed that Rózsa Flores was leading efforts to promote a separatist movement, with funding from the rightwing economic elite of Santa Cruz.
Acting attorney general José Armando Urioste announced the preliminary investigation into Morales just one week into the job on Monday.

In a letter to the supreme court, Urioste said authorities were gathering evidence against Morales and his former vice-president Álvaro García Linera “for the alleged commission of the crimes of murder, abuse, torture and unlawful detention”.
The investigation comes after a complaint filed by rightwing lawmakers Tomasa Yarhui and Rodrigo Antonio.
When the raid occurred, Morales told the press during an official visit to Venezuela that he had ordered the detention of the foreigners, whom he called “mercenaries”.
Family members and victims brought the case before the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, which concluded in 2021 that the government had violated human rights.
Neither of the accused has commented on the latest inquiry.

Morales, the first-ever Indigenous person to lead Bolivia, is currently in hiding from two active arrest warrants against him. One relates to his alleged role in massive protests that paralysed the country for 53 days earlier this year. The other accuses him of trafficking a minor with whom he is said to have had a daughter. Morales denies the allegations.
